title: Electrophysiological recordings of cardiomyocytes isolated from engineered human cardiac tissues derived from pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Prepare the papain-based dissociation solution freshly.
Incubate the dissociation solution in a 37°C water bath for 30 minutes to activate papain.
Add DNase solution (Worthington, #LS002145) at a concentration of 5 µl/mL into the papain solution before use.
Incubate 35 mm glass-bottom dishes with Geltrex coating solution for one hour at 37°C and one hour at room temperature.
Aspirate the Geltrex solution right before plating cardiomyocytes.
Wash engineered cardiac tissues with 1x PBS (phosphate buffered saline, Thermo Fisher, #70011044) twice.
Incubate the tissues in the papain-based dissociation solution containing DNase for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Gently shake the tube every two minutes during incubation.
Pipette the tissues with a 10 ml serological plastic pipette ten times after 15-minute incubation to disassociate cells.
Terminate the papain activity using serum-containing culture media.
Centrifuge the tube, aspirate all of the solution.
Wash with myocyte culture media using another centrifugation at 200xg for five minutes.
Add fresh culture media into the tube.
Replate dissociated single cardiomyocytes on the glass part of Geltrex-coated dishes.
Maintain low cell confluency (2-5%) to ensure efficient use of myocytes for electrophysiological recording conditions.
Place a dish containing sterile water next to two myocyte dishes in a 100mm dish to maintain humidity and prevent medium drying.
Add 2 ml of cardiomyocyte culture media to the dishes twenty-four hours after plating.
Two or three days after plating, wash the dishes with patch clamp external recording solution at 37°C if action potential recording is required.
Add the recording solution (~2ml/dish) at 37°C after washing.
Complete whole-cell patch clamp recordings within 2-3 days of myocyte dissociation and plating.
Find single cardiomyocytes on the dish using a 20x objective lens.
Fill the internal solution (reagent 5 for action potential recording) into a glass pipette.
Install the filled pipette into the electrode connected with the manipulator holder.
Move the pipette in the external solution using the manipulator controller at speed 0 or 1.
Examine pipette resistance.
Move the pipette tip on top of the target cell slowly using a 20x objective lens.
Confirm that there is no bubble inside the glass pipette.
Apply pressure using a 10ml syringe to get rid of bubbles and debris if observed.
Move the pipette down slowly, speed 6, to about 30μm above the cell.
Switch the objective lens to 40x.
Again confirm that pipette resistance and pressure are stable and there are no bubble or debris inside the pipette.
Switch to intermediate magnification changer 1.5X.
Use PC monitor to see the target myocyte with MetaMorph software and ECDD camera instead of 10x eyepiece of the microscope.
Seal the cell using a glass pipette with gentle mouth pressure.
Apply pressure to seal the thicker and elastic region of the target cell, but not close to the nucleus.
Maintain a holding potential at -60 mV after successful sealing (>3 GΩ).
Apply small amounts of pressure multiple times using mouth suction to break through the plasma membrane.
Measure the cell capacitance immediately after breaking through the membrane using whole cell clamp mode in pClamp 10 software.
Switch the mode to current-clamp to ensure there are no spontaneous action potentials.
Start recording action potentials.
Use reagent 6 and 8 as external and internal solutions for IK1 current recording, respectively.
Measure Ba²⁺-sensitive current by applying a 2-second voltage clamp from -130 to +10 mV (holding at -40 mV, 0.1 Hz).
Apply a 0.5 mM BaCl₂ solution for 2 minutes before and after measuring the Ba²⁺-sensitive current.
Analyze the current-voltage plot to determine the negative slope conductance consistent with inward rectification.
